newsitem.title: USA: US cash crudes step aside on sharp outright losses.
newsitem.headline: US cash crudes step aside on sharp outright losses.

text.p: Sharp losses on the NYMEX futures market have kept U.S. cash crudes weak heading into the late stages of Thursday afternoon trading.
Traders said the technical selling in the futures market, and drastic declines in the value of gas oil in London, then heating oil and gasoline in New York, have pressured the outright crude price.
Cash trade has been muted due to the busy sell-off in the paper markets.
"People stand back from the cash market when there is such a move on the futures," said a trader.

March West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was down 85 cts at $23.00-10 a barrel. March/April WTI spreads were down 5 cts from Wednesday at 34 cts, leaving Postings Plus values weaker between $2.10-15, traders said.
Other deals were heard done in the postings market at $2.17, $2.14, $2.15 and $2.16.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James remained stuck between a wide range of 15-20 cts over the WTI/Cushing, selling most prominently at a 17 cts premium.
Midland/WTI was done at 38 cts over the marker, even from Wednesday, but still much weaker than the comparable lights.
Sour grades have seen West Texas Sour/Midland trade at $2.25 and $2.28 below the benchmark.
